_schema: Recipe meta. Recipe rows live in gdd/data/recipes_part*.json (merged by gdd/tools/render_recipes.py). Row fields: id, name, unlock (must match canon C10), d (difficulty 1-5), var (price variance 0.85-1.15), prep (base prep seconds), desc, ing [[ING, qty, state]], steps [[ACTION, STN, text, T_ready?, opts?]] (opts: {c: component, flip: bool, dial: LOW|MED|HIGH, w: perfect-window s}; MIX text lists ingredients in insertion sequence; the final ASSEMBLE text lists layers bottom->top), set (true = unordered dish), core [ING], counts {ING: [n, unit]}, box (container override), loves/hates [PER], sat (extra modifier text), cx [complaints], look, anim, vfx, mut.

category_intro.BRG: The shack's backbone: burgers teach GRILL timing and stack order on day one, then mutate into fire, ice, tentacles and the frankly unreasonable. Every burger is a stacked dish, so the canonical bottom → top order below is graded.
category_intro.PIZ: Pizzas are bake-after-assembly dishes: build raw on the board, then one BAKE at `STN_PIZZA_OVEN` (spin to bake evenly) sets every topping to BAKED. Topping order only matters for mods, so the stack lists sauce-up order for the ghost guide.
category_intro.TAC: Tacos and Mexican-inspired dishes are fast, colourful and modular — shells, tortillas and chips around SAUTE-cooked fillings — and scale up into spice challenges for `PER_022` fans.
category_intro.SAN: Sandwiches are cold-or-toasted stacks: cheap, quick and order-sensitive, then increasingly architectural (bread in the middle, sandwiches made of sandwiches).
category_intro.SOP: Soups use the `STN_SOUP_POT` (one pot = 4 servings, stir to keep it Perfect) and serve in bowls, so they are always plated. Later soups freeze, scream, glow and refuse to end.
category_intro.PST: Pasta is BOIL timing plus SAUTE sauces; lasagnas are bake-after-assembly. The late pasta line is where the weird gets clever (mimic dough, infinite noodles).
category_intro.BRK: Breakfast dishes are pancake-and-egg juggling acts — batter MIX sequences, SAUTE tosses and lots of countable layers for COUNT mods.
category_intro.DES: Desserts (price ×0.8) cover cookies to cakes to things that bite back. Many are the perfect C11.5 "Peace Offering" because they are fast and cheap.
category_intro.DRK: Drinks (price ×0.7) are quick add-ons that lift the average ticket. All are served in cups (always plated), and POUR drinks can carry a drink mood for §6.18.
category_intro.SEA: Seafood brings FRY breading chains, STEAM and the first SPECIAL-stock dishes; everything fishy is cartoon-friendly (googly eyes are gummy, tentacles are squishy calamari).
category_intro.SAL: Salads (price ×0.7) are CHOP-rhythm dishes served in bowls with set matching — fast, cheap, and very important to `PER_021`.
category_intro.FRI: Fried foods (price ×0.7) are fryer rhythm: shake inside the window, watch OilHeat, skim between batches (§5.4.4).
category_intro.ALN: Alien Cuisine unlocks with the Alien Cuisine course (story chapter 5, Zorp `NPC_027`). Every dish uses at least one alien-tagged SPECIAL ingredient and most use `STN_ANTIGRAV` FLOAT-frying.
category_intro.MUT: Mutation Cuisine needs an owned `STN_INFUSER`; every dish INFUSEs mutagen. Canon C10 rule: the customer who eats it sprouts a random cosmetic mutation part for 60 s (client-visual only) and gains +10 "Whoa!" satisfaction.
category_intro.LEG: Legendary Dishes (price ×2.5) are granted only by Legendary Recipe quests (see §20), use legendary SPECIAL ingredients and span at least four processing stations — they are co-op showpieces designed for TIER_08+ kitchens.

ingredient_rules: - **Supply model (canon C9).** **BASIC** ingredients (unlock ≤ L20 and no special tag) are *unlimited*: storage fixtures dispense them on demand and their unit cost is netted from the sale when the dish is served (never paid upfront). Food thrown away is charged at `STN_TRASH`, never taking the balance below 0 MB. **SPECIAL** ingredients — tagged alien, mutagen, legendary, gold or glowing, or unlocking above L20 (all such rows carry the rarity flag) — are *stocked*: bought as crates, shelved, and consumed one unit per qty. A recipe whose SPECIAL stock has no unreserved unit shows **SOLD OUT** (§6.1.7).

- **Storage stations.** Every ingredient names one home fixture: `STN_PANTRY` (dry, jars, candy), `STN_FRIDGE` (chilled; includes the ice bin) or `STN_FREEZER` (frozen-tag SPECIAL stock; available from L5 / TIER_02, so no ingredient below L5 lives there). Taking an ingredient spawns it in state RAW in the player's hands (`ANM_006`).

- **Shelf capacity.** Only SPECIAL stock occupies capacity: 60 units per Pantry Shelf, 40 per Refrigerator, 30 per Freezer [TUNABLE]. Additional storage fixtures are furniture (§36.13) and add their capacity; fixtures do not use appliance slots (C6).

- **Crates.** SPECIAL ingredients come in crates of a fixed size (20 units for items under 10 MB, 10 for 10–40 MB, 5 or fewer for legendary stock). Crate price = size × unit cost — no bulk discount, so recipe margins in §6 are exact; the Ingredient Stocker's discount is the only reduction besides EFFICIENCY.

- **Where to buy.** Restaurant Supplies `BLD_03` (clerk Bolt Butterworth `NPC_006`) and the in-restaurant Supplies tab sell every unlocked SPECIAL crate; the Weird Produce Stand `BLD_20` (Farmer Fungus `NPC_023`) rotates three crates a day at 20 % off; the Mystery Market `BLD_13` (`NPC_015`) stocks legendary crates in its weekly rotation; offline discoveries (C15: 1 % per simulated hour) and city events can drop free crates.

- **Delivery flow.** (1) Buy a crate → `EconomyService` debits the price. (2) After 30 s the crate drops onto the `STN_DELIVERY` dock (max 4 queued). (3) The player or a Stocker carries it (one carry slot) to the matching storage fixture. (4) Interact for 1 s to unpack: units move into stock up to capacity; leftovers stay in the crate on the dock.

- **Ingredient Stocker (`ROLE_STOCKER`, C14.1).** Discount on SPECIAL crates = 5 % + 10 % × skill / 100 (5–15 %). The Stocker auto-buys crates when an ingredient falls below its par level, within the player's daily stock budget, and carries and unpacks them; offline it applies the same discount to the C15 ingredient cost.

- **No spoilage (design rule).** Ingredients never rot. Spoilage would punish players for logging off (contradicting C22 E5's no-decay rule), add timer micromanagement that is miserable on mobile, and turn SOLD OUT into a punishment rather than a planning signal. The logistics game is *quantity* and *carrying*, not freshness.

- **Kid-friendly "gross" food.** Every gross-looking ingredient is a candy or squishy version and says so in its name: gummy eyeballs, fruit slime jelly, candy Bug Crunch, gummy worms, squishy calamari-style tentacles, googly-eyed (gummy) fish. Descriptions and barks never imply real insects, real body parts or anything scary.

- **Prep states and actions.** An ingredient accepts only the C8 actions listed for it; its prep states are RAW plus the states those actions produce. The renderer rejects any recipe that applies an action an ingredient does not accept, and any required state no recipe step produces.
- **Cost at serve.** Ingredient cost actually charged = Σ qty × unit cost × (1 − 0.0015 × EFFICIENCY) (C5); mod-added ingredients are charged too, mod-removed ones are not (§6.18.5).
